root_cause.text: In `cpcap_battery_probe()`, the interrupt handler was registered (via `devm_request_irq`) before the `power_supply` was registered (via `devm_power_supply_register`), causing the `power_supply` to be freed first during driver removal and creating a race where an interrupt could call `power_supply_changed()` on a freed handle.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `cpcap_battery_init_interrupts()` after `power_supply_register()` in the probe sequence; the commit message explicitly describes the use-after-free scenario due to reversed `devm_` resource ordering.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `cpcap_battery_probe()` function (lines ~680-770) registers interrupts via `cpcap_battery_init_interrupts()` (which calls `devm_request_threaded_irq`) at line ~725, before registering the power supply via `devm_power_supply_register()` at line ~760. The interrupt handler `cpcap_battery_irq_thread()` (line ~520) calls `power_supply_changed(ddata->psy)`. Since devm resources are freed in reverse order of allocation, during driver removal the power supply will be freed before the interrupts, causing a race where an interrupt can access a freed `ddata->psy`. The `atomic_set(&ddata->active, 1)` after power supply registration does not prevent this race. No fix is present in this commit.
